overview: Implements the daily click analytics feature for active shortened links by introducing a GET /analytics/{code}/daily endpoint. The design utilizes a pre-aggregated daily counter entity (ShortLinkDailyClick) with a composite index on (ShortLinkId, Date) to guarantee fast lookups and atomic daily incrementation during redirects without modifying existing ShortLink counters. Daily queries generate a zero-filled contiguous UTC date sequence ending on the current UTC date, strictly validating the 'days' query parameter (1 to 90) and handling expired or missing links uniformly with existing analytics endpoints.

decisions.title: Pre-aggregated Daily Counters vs Individual Event Log Rows
decisions.choice: Store daily clicks in a pre-aggregated ShortLinkDailyClick table keyed uniquely on (ShortLinkId, Date).
decisions.rationale: High-traffic redirect endpoints would suffer unbounded storage growth and costly run-time GROUP BY aggregations if every click were stored as an individual row. A pre-aggregated daily counter provides O(1) upsert during redirection and O(N) bounded retrieval for up to 90 days.
alternatives: Individual ClickEvents table recording timestamp, IP, and ShortLinkId
JSON column on ShortLink containing serialized daily counts

decisions.title: In-Memory Date Range Zero-Filling
decisions.choice: Query existing records for the link between (TodayUtc - days + 1) and TodayUtc, projecting into a dictionary, then generate all N consecutive dates in C# memory zero-filling dates with no clicks.
decisions.rationale: SQLite lacks built-in calendar tables or recursive CTE convenience across all configurations. Since N is capped at 90, in-memory zero-filling is negligible in CPU and memory overhead while ensuring deterministic chronological ascending order.
alternatives: Recursive common table expression (CTE) in SQL generating calendar dates
Pre-populating 90 days of zero rows at link creation time

decisions.title: Strict Query Parameter Parsing and Validation
decisions.choice: Explicitly parse the 'days' query string parameter using int.TryParse and validate (1 <= days <= 90), returning HTTP 400 Bad Request with ErrorResponse if invalid or missing format.
decisions.rationale: Protects against unexpected inputs, injection attempts, and invalid boundary queries without bubbling unhandled exceptions.
alternatives: Default to 7 on any parsing failure
Clamp out-of-range values silently to 1 or 90

risks.risk: Concurrency conflicts or duplicate rows during simultaneous redirects on the same link on date boundaries.
risks.mitigation: Enforce a unique database constraint on (ShortLinkId, Date) and use EF Core execution strategy or database upsert logic to handle concurrent increments cleanly.

risks.risk: Database migration altering ShortLink schema or causing data loss during deployment.
risks.mitigation: Implement ShortLinkDailyClick as an independent table with an additive foreign key relationship, leaving the existing ShortLink table untouched to guarantee backwards compatibility and zero data loss.

risks.risk: Timezone skew or local clock drift causing inconsistent date categorization.
risks.mitigation: Strictly utilize UTC date calculations using DateTime.UtcNow and DateOnly.FromDateTime(DateTime.UtcNow) across all writes and queries.
